newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. team to meet Indian officials on wheat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. team to meet Indian officials on wheat.

text.p: A U.S. delegation will hold discussions this week with Indian companies and officials on wheat specifications, but the talks will not cover sales to India, a U.S. embassy spokesman said on Wednesday.
"An American wheat team is visiting India on April 24 and 25 to talk about American specifications of wheat," the spokesman told Reuters.

During its two-day visit, the U.S. team of government officials and trade representatives would meet officials of the State Trading Corporation, India's largest grain trading agency, the Food Corporation of India and the government, he said.
"There will be no negotiations on any wheat contract," the spokesman said.
Officials of state-run STC said early this month that it had contracted to import 2.74 million tonnes of wheat since December 1996, mostly from Australia, Canada and Argentina.
India banned exports of wheat in September 1996 when stock limits fell to very low levels as procurement by state agencies was four million tonnes less than estimated.
"The purpose of the visit is to explain U.S. inspection and contract procedures and explain how U.S. procedures will meet Indian requirements with respect to wheat quality," the spokesman said.
The team includes representatives of the U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Wheat Associates plus two members of private companies with extensive expertise in contract procedures.
U.S. Wheat Associates is a non-profit association representing wheat farmers and provides technical assistance to consumers.
The team would also hold discussions with Indian wheat millers and traders, the spokesman said.
